Theme

Clothes & getting dressed

tie noun

worn round the neck

also necktie, neck tie

modern

Traupman 350, 394 (focāle, p. 117)
Andresian p. 38
Traupman 117

fōcāle, fōcālis n.

noun, third declension

a necktie

Classically a neck-cloth worn by the sick or the soft (Hor. S. 2.3.255; Quint. 11.3.144; Mart. 14.142; Lewis & Short), which the lexicon also gives for a scarf; Traupman uses it for the necktie. Lewis & Short marks the ō long, from faucāle.

Examples

  • Fōcāle tibi rēctē nōdā.

    Tie your tie properly.composed

See also scarf, shirt.

SourcesLewis & Short: focale

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 117, 350, 394.

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 38.
